Thermal Insulation Materials Sectional Committee, CHD 027

FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Thermal Insulation Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. This standard was originally published in 1980. On the basis of the experience gained since its publication, the bulk density, and thermal conductivity valves have been modified in this revision to achieve a more realistic insulation design. Preformed calcium silicate insulation shall be predominantly composed of reacted hydrous calcium silicate reinforced with suitable fibres such that the physical requirements, as specified in 4, are satisfied. This standard covers preformed calcium silicate insulation for temperature up to 950�C. However, a separate standard, namely, IS 8154 : 1992 'Specification for preformed calcium silicate insulation ( for temperature up to 650�C ) ( first revision )', has also been published for preformed calcium silicate insulation suitable for temperature up to 650�C. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )' . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1 SCOPE This standard prescribes requirements and methods of sampling and test for preformed calcium silicate insulation intended for use with surfaces with reach temperature up to 950�C. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed below are necessary adjuncts to this standard: IS No. 2711 : 1979 3069 : 1992 4905 : 1968 5688 : 1970 Title Direct reading pH meters ( second revision ) Glossary of terms, symbols and units relating to thermal insulation materials Methods for random sampling Methods of test for preformed block-type and pipe covering type thermal insulation ( first revision ) Methods of test for thermal insulating cements Method of determination of thermal conductivity of insula-tion materials ( water colori-meter method ) method prescribed in 4 of IS 5688 : 1970. However, the tested value shall be in the range of 200 to 320 kg/m3. 4.2 Compressive Strength The reduction in thickness under the following conditions shall not exceed 5 percent when tested in accordance with 6 of IS 5688 : 1970: a) Dry, under a load of 415 kN/m2; and b) Wet ( after 18 hours immersion in water ), under a load of 170 kN/m2. 4.3 Flexural Strength The minimum flexural strength of the material shall be 240 kN/m2 when tested in accordance with 5 of IS 5688 : 1970. 4.4 Heat Resistance When tested in accordance with 9 of IS 5724 : 1970 and 6 of IS 5688 : 1970 at increasing tem-peratures, the material shall be deemed suitable for use under conditions of soaking heat, for 24 hours, up to the temperature at which the following requirements are met: a) Linear shrinkage ( length ), percent, Max b) Loss in mass, per-cent, Max c) Compressive strength 2 percent 15 percent Reduction in thick-ness not exceeding 5 percent under a load of 345 kN/m2

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, the definitions of terms, symbols and units given in IS 3069 : 1992 shall apply. 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Bulk Density The average bulk density of the material shall be between 220 and 280 kg/m3. 4.8 STANDARD SHAPES, SIZES AND DIMENSIONAL TOLERANCES 4.8.1 Shapes Preformed calcium silicate shall be supplied in the form of flat slabs, bevelled lags, pipe sections or radiused and bevelled lags in compliance with the requirements of 4.8.1.1 to 4.8.1.4. 4.8.1.1 Flat blocks These shall be free from warp. All mating faces shall be plane and edges shall be square to the surfaces and to one another. 4.8.1.2 Bevelled lags These shall correspond with length of standard blocks with major width from 75 mm to 166 mm in standard thickness of the flat blocks.

4.8.3.1 Uniformity The local thickness of the preformed thermal insulation material at any point shall not vary from the average thickness by more than � 3 mm.

5.2.1 The material or the package may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 6 SAMPLING The method of sampling shall be as prescribed in Annex C.

ANNEX A ( Clause 4.6 )
DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE CONTENT A-1 PROCEDURE Weigh accurately a test specimen. This speci-men shall then be dried in a ventilated oven at a temperature of 105 � 2�C until the mass becomes constant between successive weighings made at an interval of not less than 1 hour. A-2 CALCULATION Moisture content, percentage ( oven-dry mass ) = 100 �
where M1 = initial mass, in g, of the test speci-men, and Mo = oven-dry mass, in g, of the test specimen.

TEST FOR ALKALINITY B-3 PROCEDURE B-1 APPARATUS B-1.1 pH Meter B-3.1 Weigh 2 g of the crushed sample and Standard laboratory pH meter ( see IS 2711 : shake well for 10 minutes with 100 ml of dis-1977 ). tilled water at room temperature. Leave to settle for 5 minutes and measure the pH of the B-2 PREPARATION OF SAMPLE mixture using a standard pH meter and decant B-2.1 From the bulk sample, cut five pieces of the solution if necessary. Repeat the test on a approximately 5 g mass each, mass 5 g, from further 2 g of the sample and report the mean separate units. Crush these pieces and mix pH value. thoroughly.

4

IS 9428 : 1993 C-1.3.1 These units shall be selected at random. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, procedures given in IS 4905 : 1968 may be followed. C-2 NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY C-2.1 Shape, Size and Dimensions From each of the units selected from the lot according to col 1 and 2 of Table 1, one item shall be taken at random. Each of these items shall be examined for visual and dimensional characteristics given in 4.8. An item failing to satisfy any of these requirements shall be consi-dered as defective. The lot shall be considered to have satisfied these requirements if the number of defectives found in the sample is less than or equal to the corresponding acceptance number given in col 3 of Table 1. The lot having been found satisfactory for these requirements shall be further tested for bulk density, heat resis-tance, moisture content and alkalinity ( see C-2.2 ). C-2.2 Bulk Density, Moisture Content, Alkalinity and Heat Resistance The number of items given in col 4 of Table 1 shall be taken from those already tested and found satisfactory under C-2.1. These items shall be tested for bulk density ( see 4.1 ), moisture content ( see 4.6 ), alkalinity ( see 4.7 ) and heat resistance ( see 4.4 ). An item failing to satisfy any of these requirements shall be considered as defective. The lot shall be considered to have met these requirements if the number of defectives found in the sample is less than or equal to the corresponding acceptance number given in col 5 of Table 1. The lot having met these requirements shall be further tested for compressive strength and flexural strength ( see C-2.3 ). C-2.3 Compressive Strength and Flexural Strength The number of items given in col 6 of Table I shall be taken from those already examined and found satisfactory under C-2.1. These items shall be tested for compressive strength ( see 4.2 ) and flexural strength ( see 4.3 ). Any item failing to meet any of these requirements shall be considered as defective. The lot shall be deemed to have met these requirements if the number of defectives found in the sample is less than or equal to the corresponding acceptance number given in col 7 of Table 1. The lot which has been found to have met these requirements shall be finally tested for thermal conductivity ( see C-2.4 ). C-2.4 Thermal Conductivity The number of items given in col 8 of Table 1 shall be taken from those already examined and found satisfactory under C-2.1. The lot shall be declared as conforming to the require-ments of the specification if none of the samples tested for thermal conductivity fails, otherwise not.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. Revision of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 'BIS Handbook and 'Standards Monthly Additions'.
